_comment: Synthetic DDx-annotation demonstration. Every case, note, candidate list, prediction, rationale and rating is invented for this repository; none comes from MIMIC-IV or from the study. Build with: python scripts/build_synthetic_ddx_demo.py

cases.demonstrates: Pilot, train split. The cosine reference, the ICD reference and the rater agree.

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 64-year-old man felt pressure-like central chest discomfort while carrying shopping upstairs. It eased after twenty minutes of rest but returned twice overnight, each time with sweating.
note.exam: Comfortable at rest. Heart rate 88, blood pressure 152/90. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Lungs clear. Chest wall not tender.
note.results: First troponin mildly raised, second troponin higher. ECG: new ST depression in the lateral leads.
note.course: Treated with aspirin, a second antiplatelet agent and heparin. Angiography showed a tight lesion in one coronary artery, which was stented. No further pain.
note.dd: Primary: non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. Secondary: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
note.labs: Troponin rising on repeat. Creatinine and potassium within range.

findings.Acute coronary syndrome: exertional pressure with sweating, a rising troponin and new lateral ST depression
findings.Stable angina: exertional discomfort relieved by rest, although the troponin rise argues against a stable pattern
findings.Pulmonary embolism: chest discomfort without hypoxia or leg swelling makes embolism less likely

cases.demonstrates: Pilot, train split. The cosine reference (first candidate) differs from the ICD reference; the rater sides with the ICD reference.
icd: Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with other respiratory manifestations

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 51-year-old teacher developed a dry cough, fever to 39.2 and aching muscles two days after several pupils in her class fell ill. She feels exhausted and short of breath on stairs.
note.exam: Flushed, temperature 38.9. Oxygen saturation 95% on room air. Scattered wheeze, no focal crackles.
note.results: Rapid antigen swab positive for influenza A. Chest X-ray without consolidation.
note.course: Started on an antiviral and given fluids. Blood sugars were higher than usual and settled with a temporary insulin scale. Fever resolved on day three.
note.dd: Influenza A with bronchitic symptoms. Type 2 diabetes.
note.labs: White cell count normal. Glucose raised on admission.

findings.Influenza: abrupt fever with myalgia, a classroom exposure and a positive influenza A swab
findings.Acute bronchitis: a cough with wheeze but no consolidation
findings.Community-acquired pneumonia: fever and cough, although the chest X-ray shows no consolidation

cases.demonstrates: Pilot, test split. The rater marks two diagnoses (multi-label): the main one and a complication documented in the note.
icd: Calculus of gallbladder with acute cholecystitis without obstruction
Calculus of bile duct without cholangitis or cholecystitis without obstruction

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 47-year-old woman has had constant pain under the right ribs for a day, worse after a fatty meal, with vomiting and shivers.
note.pmh: Obesity. Previous episodes of milder upper abdominal pain after meals.
note.exam: Temperature 38.4. Tender in the right upper quadrant with a positive Murphy sign. No guarding elsewhere.
note.results: Ultrasound: thickened gallbladder wall with stones and pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct mildly dilated; a stone was later seen on MRCP.
note.course: Given antibiotics. The duct stone was removed endoscopically, and the gallbladder was taken out laparoscopically two days later.
note.labs: White cell count raised. Bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase mildly raised. Lipase normal.

findings.Acute cholecystitis: right upper quadrant pain after a fatty meal, fever, a positive Murphy sign and a thickened gallbladder with stones
findings.Choledocholithiasis: a dilated bile duct with raised bilirubin and a stone on MRCP
findings.Acute pancreatitis: upper abdominal pain, but the lipase is normal

cases.demonstrates: Pilot, test split. A dangerous diagnosis ranked low by the cosine score but chosen by the rater and the ICD reference.
icd: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage from unspecified intracranial artery
Migraine, unspecified, not intractable, without status migrainosus

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 39-year-old man with a history of migraine had a sudden, explosive headache while lifting weights, the worst of his life, followed by neck stiffness and one episode of vomiting.
note.pmh: Migraine without aura, a few attacks a year.
note.exam: Drowsy but oriented. Neck stiff. Pupils equal. No limb weakness.
note.results: CT head: blood in the basal cisterns. CT angiography: small aneurysm on an anterior circulation artery.
note.course: Transferred to the neurosurgical unit; the aneurysm was coiled. Nimodipine was given for three weeks. He recovered without deficit.
note.dd: Subarachnoid hemorrhage from a ruptured aneurysm. History of migraine.
note.labs: Sodium low on day five, corrected with fluid management.

findings.Subarachnoid hemorrhage: a thunderclap headache on exertion with neck stiffness and blood in the basal cisterns on CT
findings.Migraine: a known migraine history, but the onset is sudden and the pain unlike his usual attacks
findings.Bacterial meningitis: neck stiffness, but there is no fever and the CT shows blood

cases.demonstrates: 350-case study. Three raters; rater 1 marks a second, related diagnosis, raters 2 and 3 mark only the main one. Shows the WikiDoc-style diagnosis help card.

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 68-year-old man has had worsening low back pain for three weeks, now waking him at night, with sweats. Two months ago he was treated for an infected foot ulcer.
note.exam: Temperature 38.1. Marked tenderness over the third lumbar vertebra. Leg power and sensation normal; no saddle numbness.
note.results: MRI spine: signal change in two adjacent lumbar vertebral bodies and the disc between them; a small rim of enhancing tissue in front of the spinal canal without cord compression. Blood cultures grew Staphylococcus aureus.
note.course: Treated with six weeks of intravenous antibiotics through a long line. Pain improved and inflammatory markers fell. Spinal surgeons advised no operation.
note.dd: Lumbar vertebral osteomyelitis and discitis with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia. Small epidural phlegmon.
note.labs: CRP and ESR markedly raised. White cell count raised.

findings.Vertebral osteomyelitis: night pain with fever, focal vertebral tenderness, MRI changes in adjacent vertebrae and Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia
findings.Spinal epidural abscess: enhancing epidural tissue on MRI, although there is no neurological deficit
findings.Lumbar disc herniation: back pain, but fever, night pain and bacteremia point to infection

cases.demonstrates: 350-case study. The correct diagnosis is not in the candidate list: rater 1 adds it as an 'Other Disease', rater 2 marks the same added diagnosis, rater 3 marks the closest listed candidate.
icd: Adverse effect of antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs, initial encounter

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 58-year-old woman receiving immunotherapy for melanoma has had eight watery stools a day for five days, with cramping and some blood.
note.pmh: Metastatic melanoma, on a checkpoint inhibitor for four months.
note.exam: Heart rate 104. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender, no peritonism.
note.results: Stool tests for Clostridioides difficile and bacterial pathogens negative. Flexible sigmoidoscopy: inflamed colonic mucosa; biopsies showed an immune-mediated colitis pattern.
note.course: Immunotherapy paused. High-dose steroids started with rapid improvement, then a slow taper. Oncology to review restarting treatment.
note.dd: Immune checkpoint inhibitor colitis. Metastatic melanoma.

findings.Medication-induced diarrhea: watery diarrhea starting during checkpoint-inhibitor treatment with negative stool infection tests
findings.Clostridioides difficile infection: acute watery diarrhea, but the toxin test is negative
findings.Ulcerative colitis: bloody diarrhea with colonic inflammation, although the timing follows immunotherapy

cases.demonstrates: 350-case study. Raters 1 and 3 agree; rater 2 has not annotated this case (incomplete overlap).
icd: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 77-year-old woman has been increasingly breathless over a week, now cannot lie flat, and her ankles have swollen. She ran out of her water tablets ten days ago.
note.pmh: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. Atrial fibrillation. Chronic kidney disease.
note.exam: Oxygen saturation 89% on room air. Irregular pulse 112. Raised jugular venous pressure, crackles at both bases, pitting oedema to the knees.
note.results: Chest X-ray: enlarged heart, upper lobe venous diversion, small bilateral effusions. Echo: ejection fraction 25%, unchanged.
note.course: Intravenous diuretics with four litres of fluid removed over five days. Rate control adjusted. Discharged on her usual tablets with a written plan for daily weights.
note.dd: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure after stopping diuretics. Atrial fibrillation. Chronic kidney disease stage 3.
note.labs: BNP markedly raised. Creatinine slightly above her baseline.

findings.Acute decompensated heart failure: orthopnoea, ankle oedema, raised venous pressure, bibasal crackles and a raised BNP after stopping diuretics
findings.Pleural effusion: small bilateral effusions, best explained by the heart failure
findings.Pneumonia: crackles and breathlessness, but no fever and no consolidation

cases.demonstrates: 350-case study. The cosine reference (acute coronary syndrome) and the ICD reference (pulmonary embolism) disagree; both raters side with the ICD reference.
icd: Other pulmonary embolism without acute cor pulmonale
Acute embolism and thrombosis of unspecified deep veins of right lower extremity

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 33-year-old woman, three weeks after a long-haul flight and a sprained ankle in a cast, has sharp right-sided chest pain on breathing in and is breathless walking to the bathroom.
note.exam: Heart rate 118, oxygen saturation 92% on room air. Right calf swollen and tender. Chest clear.
note.results: CT pulmonary angiogram: clots in segmental arteries of the right lower lobe. Leg ultrasound: deep vein thrombosis. ECG: sinus tachycardia only. Troponin normal.
note.course: Started on anticoagulation, switched to a tablet before discharge. The contraceptive pill was stopped and alternatives discussed.
note.dd: Pulmonary embolism with right leg deep vein thrombosis.

findings.Pulmonary embolism: pleuritic pain and breathlessness after immobilisation, tachycardia, low oxygen saturation and a swollen calf
findings.Acute coronary syndrome: chest pain, but the troponin is normal and the ECG shows only sinus tachycardia
findings.Pneumothorax: pleuritic pain and breathlessness, but the chest is clear on examination

cases.demonstrates: 350-case study. Raters 1 and 2 disagree (pneumonia vs COPD exacerbation).

note.hpi: SYNTHETIC CASE - not a real patient. A 71-year-old man with COPD has had more cough and green sputum for four days, a fever since yesterday and new pain on the left side when he coughs.
note.pmh: COPD, uses inhalers; two flare-ups last year. Ex-smoker of forty pack-years.
note.exam: Temperature 38.6, oxygen saturation 90% on room air. Wheeze throughout and bronchial breathing at the left base.
note.results: Chest X-ray: consolidation in the left lower lobe. Sputum culture: Streptococcus pneumoniae.
note.course: Treated with antibiotics, nebulisers and a short course of steroids. Oxygen weaned by day four.
note.dd: Left lower lobe pneumonia. COPD with exacerbation.
note.labs: White cell count and CRP raised.

findings.Community-acquired pneumonia: fever, pleuritic pain, bronchial breathing and left lower lobe consolidation with pneumococcus in the sputum
findings.COPD exacerbation: more cough, purulent sputum and wheeze in a man with COPD
findings.Acute bronchitis: productive cough, although the consolidation indicates pneumonia
